description: Around the year 1000 your mother Esther's spell made you and your siblings the first vampires, the Originals.  Every vampire walking the earth descends from your bloodline.  You are stronger and faster than any of them, you heal almost instantly, and you can compel vampires as easily as humans.  You no longer need food or water: the only thing your body asks for is blood.  Like every vampire you burn in the sun: without your daylight ring, daylight will kill you slowly.

descriptions.text: You hear a strong, rhythmic human heartbeat and smell warm arterial blood pulsing through veins here.
You hear the faint, steady pulse of a creature here.

name.str: The Curse of the Sun and the Moon

description: You are the bastard son of a werewolf, Ansel, and when your first kill proved it your mother bound your wolf side with the curse of the sun and the moon.  For a thousand years it has slept inside you, and you have hunted for the way to break it: the moonstone, a witch, a vampire, a werewolf, and the blood of the Petrova doppelganger.  You can't turn.  Under the moon you can feel the wolf pacing in its cage.

Fire, stakes, decapitation: none of it keeps an Original down for long.  Your thousand-year-old indestructible nervous system and hybrid constitution grant virtually complete pain insensitivity (-85% pain, -95% pain penalties), though toxic wood embedded in your flesh disrupts this immunity until removed.  No matter how battered or pierced your flesh is, your absolute mental concentration remains unbroken, ensuring you can always focus to unleash your ancient hybrid powers.

Your god-tier immortal physiology continuously mends broken bones, knits shattered flesh, and seals hemorrhaging wounds scaled directly by the volume of stolen blood stored in your veins (up to +10 HP every 3s).  Only a stake carved from the white oak tree driven through your heart can end an Original for good.

White oak is death to an Original, and silver daggers dipped in white oak ash put you into a dead sleep until someone pulls them out.  You can hardly stand to touch the stuff.  (Carrying white oak makes you uneasy.)

The Mikaelsons' vow to one another, a thousand years old.  You love your family more than anything in the world, and you've daggered every one of them at least once for disloyalty.  Keeping the coffins of your siblings close steadies you.  Betrayal is the one thing you never forgive.

You've painted for centuries and you're very, very good at it.  You studied under the masters of the Renaissance and you still sketch obsessively.  Drawing in your sketchbook or finishing a painting calms the rage inside you.
